findings.title: Clay, creation, and the measure of worth
findings.claim: The focus's clay origin becomes a measure of worth in the wider account where Iblis says he is better because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay. Other supplied accounts place clay beside good making, proportioned form, and spirit, so the material clause remains intact while the wider echoes expose the ranking built on it.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries creation at 17:61:12 and clay at 17:61:13, with Iblis asking about prostration at 17:61:10. The exact 38:76 connection makes the superiority claim explicit; 2:34 names the refusal as self-exaltation; 32:7 and 15:29 return human creation to good making, form, and spirit; 7:11 and 82:7 add formed and proportioned creation. These contacts return through the focus's clay, creation, and prostration words, making material origin one side of a comparison rather than a complete measure of the created person.
findings.reader_payoff: The question becomes legible as an argument that ranks two origins, while the wider creation accounts show why clay can remain the material beginning without exhausting the human form or standing.
findings.containment: The focus still asks whether Iblis should prostrate to one created from clay. The wider parallels add a material ranking and a formed-creation counterpoint without replacing that wording. The measure facet is a contextual echo of proportioning, and the bodily-bending facet is analogical; neither makes every available root sense active.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run publication supplies the core claim and focus anchors. Exact target Arabic and connection notes ground the wider comparison, but target morphology is not supplied and the measure and bodily-posture facets are contextual rather than literal translations.
